scope.description: Two VerifyLeader invocations on real five-member in-memory clusters. Both bootstrap five voters, demote two non-leader members to non-voters, and disconnect the leader's transport from the two remaining voters in both directions. The trigger leaves the two non-voters reachable; the control also disconnects them. Each case records the reachable member counts, the voter quorum, whether the verification completed and with what error, and the leader state afterwards.
assumptions: All members run the captured code on the in-memory transport with one-second heartbeat, election and lease timeouts so the leader is not stepped down by the lease check during the short window.
Disconnect removes routing in both directions, modelling a partition that isolates the leader from those members only.
The verification is bounded by a two-second wait; a verification that never completes is reported as completed=false rather than failing the harness.
The demotions are committed through the leader before the partition; the harness does not separately assert each member's view of the new configuration.
excluded: No claim about read serializability beyond what VerifyLeader itself promises; the harness does not issue reads.
No transfer or configuration change during the partition, and no client traffic.

basis.prefix: Each case builds a five-voter in-memory cluster through MakeClusterCustom with one-second heartbeat, election and lease timeouts, waits for a leader, demotes two non-leader members with DemoteVoter, and sleeps 300 ms. It then disconnects the leader's transport from the two remaining voters in both directions and, in the control only, from the two non-voters as well. The case event records member counts and the voter quorum; the harness calls leader.VerifyLeader(), waits up to two seconds for the future, and emits whether it completed, whether it returned nil, its error text and the leader's state afterwards.
basis.responsibility: VerifyLeader is documented as protecting against stale reads after leadership has been lost, so the library owns the definition of the support that satisfies it. The quorum it sizes is a voter quorum, and the messages it counts must therefore be voter acknowledgements; a non-voter cannot contribute to leadership legitimacy.

comparisons.description: Control: with no reachable supporter the verification must not report success.
With only one of three voters reachable against a quorum of two, the verification must not report success; a true value contradicts it.
